description: Compare monitors before and after a deploy, without running any check. For each monitor it compares the checks since `since` with the 24 hours before it, per region, and returns verdict PASS, REGRESSED (most regions slower or failing more than in the baseline, or one region failing), FAIL (most regions failing now, or an incident opened since `since`) or INSUFFICIENT_DATA (too few checks yet: wait `retry_after_seconds` and call again; or too little history: say so and stop). These verdicts are not monitor statuses: REGRESSED is not the DEGRADED of list_monitors. Checks run inside a maintenance window count by their result. Each monitor lists its regions with check counts, the median latency since the deploy and the baseline p95 (for HTTP monitors the comparison uses time to first byte when both sides have it; each region's latency_metric says which), plus incidents_since, changes_since (outside changes such as DNS or certificate) and needs_fresh_checks (call check_now on it before retrying). Paused monitors come back in `skipped`, and deploy markers near `since` in `deploy_markers`. Select monitors with `monitor_ids` or with `tag` (+ `tag_match`), never both, at most 100. check_now allows 10 calls a minute, so with many monitors call check_now first on those whose interval_seconds is over 60: the faster ones fill up on their own schedule. Pass the same `since` on every retry. When retry_after_seconds is null, stop: it turns null 15 minutes after `since` at the latest. The tool only reads: for fresh points call check_now first. A 5xx on a large selection that repeats after one retry means the check is too large: pass fewer monitors or a later `since`. Limited to 10 calls per minute per calling address for an API key, per user for an app connection (never per key or organization); past that it is a 429 with the seconds to wait. Example: {"tag": ["service:api"], "since": "2026-11-01T10:02:00Z"}

monitor_ids.description: 1 to 100 distinct monitor uuids from list_monitors. A repeated id is a 422 and an unknown id is a 404 naming it. Not with tag.

since.description: When the deploy finished, ISO 8601 with a UTC offset, for example 2026-11-01T10:02:00Z. At most 24 hours ago; up to 5 minutes ahead is read as now. A time without an offset is a 422. Use the deployed_at you gave record_deploy.

tag.description: Keep items carrying these tags: a JSON array of up to 10 tags, each up to 50 characters, lowercased before matching. tag_match decides whether all or any of them must match. At most 100 monitors (paused included) may match. Not with monitor_ids.

tag_match.description: all (the default): an item must carry every tag in tag. any: at least one of them.

name: verify_deploy

deploy_markers.description: Up to 5 recorded deploys near `since` that touched these monitors.

compare_url.description: Link to the diff, when one was given.

ref.description: Commit SHA, tag or branch recorded with the deploy.

latency_metric.description: The latency every region was compared on, or mixed when regions differ; each region row names its own; response_time_ms when no monitor was compared. Known values: response_time_ms, ttfb_ms, mixed.

monitors.description: Judged monitors, worst verdict first, then by name.

changes_since.description: Up to 10 detected changes since the deploy, newest first.

confidence.description: How sure the detection is. Known values: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW.

first_seen_at.description: When the change was first seen.

reverted_at.description: When the change reverted; null while it is in effect.

severity.description: How serious the change is. Known values: INFO, NOTICE.

signal.description: What changed (for example a certificate). Known values: DNS_ANSWERS, CERTIFICATE, REDIRECT, RESPONSE_HEADER.

incidents_since.description: Up to 10 incidents that started after the deploy, newest first.

cause.description: Structured cause of the incident. Known values: TIMEOUT, DNS_FAILURE, CONNECTION_REFUSED, TLS_INVALID, HTTP_4XX, HTTP_5XX, HTTP_UNEXPECTED_STATUS, KEYWORD_MISSING, TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, TARGET_BLOCKED, PORT_STATE_MISMATCH, INVALID_TARGET, HEARTBEAT_MISSED, HEARTBEAT_FAILED, UNKNOWN.

incident_id.description: Incident id; use get_incident for details.

resolved_at.description: When it recovered; null while it is open.

needs_fresh_checks.description: True when a manual check of this monitor would speed up the answer.

reasons.description: Why the verdict was given; empty for PASS.

items.description: Known values: INCIDENT_OPENED, REGIONS_FAILING, REGION_FAILING, REGIONS_SLOWER, REGIONS_ERRORS, FEW_CHECKS, NO_BASELINE, MONITOR_PAUSED.

regions.description: One entry per configured region, in the monitor's order.

baseline_checks.description: Checks in the 24 closed hours before the deploy's hour, outside maintenance windows.

baseline_failing_ratio.description: Share of baseline checks that failed; null without a baseline.

baseline_p95_ms.description: 95th percentile latency of the baseline, in the region's latency_metric; null without one.

checks.description: Checks since the deploy, maintenance ones included.

failing_checks.description: Of those, how many were DOWN or ERROR.

finding.description: Judgement of this region. Known values: OK, SLOWER, ERRORS, FAILING, INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

anyOf.description: Known values: UP, DEGRADED, DOWN, ERROR.

last_status.description: Status of the newest check since the deploy; null when none.

latency_metric.description: Which latency window_p50_ms and baseline_p95_ms carry: ttfb_ms (time to first byte) for an HTTP region when both sides have it, otherwise response_time_ms. Known values: response_time_ms, ttfb_ms.

maintenance_checks.description: Of those, how many ran inside a maintenance window.

region.description: Region code, as configured on the monitor.

window_p50_ms.description: Median latency since the deploy, in the region's latency_metric; null when none responded.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before checking again; null when waiting will not help.

type.description: Monitor type. Known values: HTTP, PING, SSL, TCP, DNS.

verdict.description: PASS, REGRESSED, FAIL or INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Known values: PASS, REGRESSED, FAIL, INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

retry_after_seconds.description: Largest wait among monitors that waiting can help; null when none.

since.description: The deploy time used (never later than evaluated_at).

skipped.description: Selected monitors that were not judged, such as paused ones.

reason.description: Why it was skipped (MONITOR_PAUSED). Known values: INCIDENT_OPENED, REGIONS_FAILING, REGION_FAILING, REGIONS_SLOWER, REGIONS_ERRORS, FEW_CHECKS, NO_BASELINE, MONITOR_PAUSED.

verdict.description: Worst verdict of the monitors; INSUFFICIENT_DATA when none were judged. Known values: PASS, REGRESSED, FAIL, INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

title: Compare monitors before and after a deploy
